findings.finding: Key: For triangle with BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁, geometry forces a unique s where B,K,N,K′ cyclic. Computed ratio R = (CT·NB)/(BT·NE) = Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. Hence aₙ = Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. For even n, a₂ₙ → φ³ = 2+√5. So α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5. Compute ⌊2^{5²}⌋=2²⁵=33 554 432. Mod 99991 = 57447. Pitfalls: ensure s>Fₙ₊₂, solve cyclic condition (det=0) → unique root; verify ratio matches closed form.

Model triangle with BC=F_{n+2}, BD=F_n, CD=F_{n+1}. Use incircle: tan(B/2)=r/F_n, tan(C/2)=r/F_{n+1}. Impose cyclic K‑N‑K'‑B → unique r solving gives ratio CT·NB/(BT·NE)=F_{n+2}/F_{n-1}. Hence a_{2n}=F_{2n+2}/F_{2n-1}→α=lim=φ³=2+√5. Compute floor(2^{5²}) mod 99991 = 57447.
